The scalar joint-law construction provides finite-valued nonnegative versions everywhere, so every finite sampled weight sum and normalization is defined. Scheme choice is supplied per transition. Both all-zero branches return a probability vector; zero Z remains zero. The finite loop returns the path empirical measure and product normalizer, including t=0. Repeated resampling calls have a supplier edge and no self-edge. No accuracy or convergence claim is asserted. Accept the reader input clarification. Reviewed all six steps, every cited interface and the reader preimage delta. Finite resampling probabilities, Borel floor/normalization branches, finite product proposal kernels and finite mixtures define the particle law. Null-history avoidance is proved for each fixed Q-null set before using marginal-a.e. derivative identities. Conditional expected offspring counts suffice for both schemes; child independence across ancestors is not assumed. The identity Zhat_k wbar_k^i = Zhat_(k-1) a_k^i/N handles the zero-sum branch exactly, and zero accumulated Zhat kills all subsequent mass. Nonnegative conditional-kernel integration precedes L1 conditional expectation, avoiding circular integrability. The induction applies to g_k because its gamma integral equals the finite gamma_k(phi); t=0 and phi=1 are valid. Infinite test values on target-null sets use zero-times-infinity and a.e. finite representatives before L1/tower. The N-in-N and 0<=t clarification agrees with the existing finite algorithm.
